fields.walk_rule.text: Rule: callers whose body calls helper by bare name or import alias, except a call its imports bind to no file defining helper (json.loads is no caller of a project loads); level k+1 looks each caller up by name carrying its definition site; explicit imports label module-level function targets without filtering candidates, same-named candidates still join; each (file, caller) once; depth 1 (1..5). Measured: levels 1 and 2.

standing: Dynamic dispatch (getattr/setattr, importlib, eval/exec) is not resolved.
Method resolution order (MRO) is not considered.
Calls via importlib/dynamic imports are not tracked.
Calls inside string-evaluated code (eval/exec) are not detected.

Top-level caller scopes are indexed for Python, JS/TS, PHP and Ruby source files; module calls retain file/line provenance. Class-body initializers, extensionless Ruby DSL files and top-level scopes in other languages are outside this relationship scope.

fields.walk_rule.text: Rule: callees by definition: each definition of the name, then each definition a call reaches, is expanded once, at its shallowest level; every call site of an expanded definition is an edge (call text de-duplicated per definition); a call resolves within the caller's language family to its one definition, except that a call through an import that resolves to no project file is external; else a same-file one or the one its imports name, else it is ambiguous and not expanded; builtins hidden (--builtins shows them); depth 1 (1..5). Measured: depth-1 call lists only.

'Uncalled' is a derived heuristic, not a separately measured signal, so it carries no confidence: call extraction is measured, dead code is not, and every convention-invoked call static analysis cannot see (runtime constructors, framework lifecycle hooks, dynamic dispatch) is also missing. Zero callers found is not proof of dead code.
Excludes __dunder__ methods and @property/@classmethod/@staticmethod (implicitly invoked, not statically reachable).
